findings.view: scene-synthetic.png, synthetic-chain.png, synthetic-chain-intercept.png, scene-synthetic-intercept.png, synthetic-8-patches.png (return legs x 495-640, y 365-620; crop x 520-600, y 470-580 at 7x); synthetic-moon-intercept.png (orange dashed patch from the AN diamond (905,569) to the small SOI marker (1015,486))
findings.defect: On the long-range planned patches each dash is drawn as two overlaid partial patterns: a full-strength piece, then a dim brown piece offset from it, then a ghost tail. The line reads as dash, half-dash, ghost rather than one rhythm. A trace along the single orange strand in synthetic-moon-intercept.png, at about 1 px per sample, gives one 26 px period as: 7 px at R 186, 4 px at R 110-170, 3 px at R 186, 5 px at R 22-84, and only 4 px of true gap at R 1. The dim fraction drifts along the strand (R 22 to 84 in one gap, 167 to 110 in the other), so the pattern visibly changes along the path. Short-range dashes are clean: lowOrbit-node.png at 6x and real-hud-lowOrbit-node-4k.png. The fault is on the Earth-Moon legs that the overview exists to show.
findings.realReference: KSP / KSP 2 / Juno: New Origins draw a planned patch with one dash rhythm at every zoom. The gaps are as empty as the background, and nothing mid-tone sits between dashes.
findings.likelyCause: The hand-off's 'Known limits' says dashes cross-fade between two octaves of world period by depth, so a stretch at a depth between octaves shows both patterns at partial strength. A patch hundreds of thousands of km long crosses several octaves, so most of the overview sits in a blend. The two octaves' dash and gap intervals do not nest, so the blend fills the gaps with partial dashes.
findings.fixDirection: Make the octaves nest so a blend can only fill a gap fully or not at all. One option: define the coarse pattern's dashes as unions of fine dashes (fine period P with dash 0.6P; coarse period 2P where the dash covers [0, 1.6P) and the gap [1.6P, 2P) coincides with a fine gap), then cross-fade only the second fine gap. Another option: pick one world period per line piece from its mean m/px and switch it with hysteresis on zoom instead of per fragment. Add a pixel check in screens.spec.ts that every sample along a planned patch in scene-synthetic is either at least 0.8 of the dash peak or within 10 levels of the background.

findings.defect: Two different planned legs that run 3-5 px apart are each drawn with their own casing and unrelated dash phase. Pink dashes sit beside and between orange ones, forming a jagged ladder rather than two parallel lines, and on the Earth disc it reads as one broken stroke. This is the leftover of round-1 A1, which the hand-off admits (coincidence threshold 3 px).
findings.realReference: KSP 2 draws two nearly coincident patches either as one stroke or as two lines clearly separated in phase and spacing; never as interleaved short dashes.
findings.likelyCause: suppressCoincident only merges within 3 px. Dash phase is measured from each patch's own node, so neighbouring legs from different nodes have unrelated phases.
findings.fixDirection: For pairs that stay within 3-6 px over more than two dash periods, align the second line's phase to the first (take the arc parameter at the nearest point of the earlier line). Or offset it to a clear 2-line-width separation. Or draw it as a thin solid line with no dashes.

findings.view: accept-node-added.png -> accept-prograde-drag.png -> accept-panel.png (pad label 'Ka Lae Pacific Spaceport, Launch Complex 1'); accept-panel.png (vessel leader x 715-745, y 290-318)
findings.defect: Between two consecutive acceptance frames the pad label jumps. It was in empty space right of the pad (x 742-1000, y 445-460) and moves below-left (x 597-857, y 449-464) over the disc, covering the yellow dashed planned orbit and the green zone ring. Only the prograde field changed (0 to 10 m/s), which moves the planned path by under a pixel at this zoom. The label stays in the worse place in accept-panel.png. While a handle is dragged this will flicker. In accept-panel.png the 'Fake vessel' leader also runs under the selected node's anti-normal handle.
findings.realReference: Shipped map labels keep their position while their anchor is still and only move when the old position becomes blocked.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/labels.ts declutter is a stateless greedy search every frame (rank plus LINE_COST * line cost, no memory of the previous choice). Small changes in the line cost under a candidate flip the winner.
findings.fixDirection: Keep each label's previous candidate (by id) unless it is blocked or a new one is cheaper by a margin (about 2 ranks). Treat gizmo handles and arms as obstacles for leaders. Record the drag sequence and assert that a label whose anchor moved less than 1 px does not move.

findings.view: real-hud-lowOrbit-node-720p.png ('Ap 1839.1km' x 350-430, y 538-552, beside the HUD's 'APOAPSIS 200.0 km'); lowOrbit-node.png and real-lowOrbit-node.png ('Ap 1839.1km'); accept-panel.png ('Ap 371.5km' x 568-640, y 418-431 next to 'Ap 200.0 km' x 449-525, y 445-457); accept-zoom-200km.png and real-lowOrbit*.png ('Pe 200.0km')
findings.defect: At 720p the narrow no-break spaces collapse. Measured column gaps: group gap 2 px against 1 px between digits, and unit gap 1-3 px depending on the label. So 'Ap 1 839.1 km' reads as 'Ap 1839.1km' and 'Pe 200.0 km' as 'Pe 200.0km'. Two labels in one frame space their units differently (accept-panel.png), and the HUD panel beside them writes '200.0 km' with a 3 px gap and '6 084 km' grouped. Uneven per-glyph spacing also crowds 'T− 1:18:20'. At 4K the spacing is right (10 px group gap, HUD 9 px). The round-3 hand-off quotes 'Ap 1 839.1 km', which the 720p pictures do not show.
findings.realReference: The flight HUD in the same frame, and any shipped interface: grouping and unit spaces stay visible at every size.
findings.likelyCause: src/map/gpu/overlayRenderer.ts writeRun snaps each glyph to Math.round(pen). The U+202F advance is about 1.9 device px at 720p, so the visible gap is 1-3 px depending on the fractional pen position and the side bearings of proportional digits.
findings.fixDirection: Give U+202F a minimum advance of about 0.25 em (3 px at 720p), as the browser renders it in the HUD. Or round the run origin once and place glyphs at fractional offsets with a subpixel atlas. Add a unit test that the rendered U+202F gap exceeds the inter-digit gap by at least 1.5 px at uiScale 1.
